title: Balance the scale
_map: Balance the scale (Y2). Big idea: <, > and = compare amounts. Creative: balance with different mixes of blocks; how many ways?
_story: Steve's market scale is wonky. Heavier side goes down; he learns the signs by watching, then balances 15 blocks every way he can with 5-blocks and 1-blocks, and catches Steve reading the sign backwards.
_stepChain: a balance scale: heavier goes down → same amount balances → = means the same → the sign's open side faces the bigger amount: > and < → many mixes can balance the same amount → Steve reads 8 < 5

talk.ask: How can you tell which side of a balance has more?
talk.goodAnswer: the heavier side goes down; if they're the same, it balances flat.

talk.ask: How do you remember which way round < and > go?
talk.goodAnswer: the open, wide side faces the bigger number; the point faces the smaller one.

handsOn: Make a balance from a coat hanger and two cups. Put Lego bricks in each cup. Can you make it balance with big bricks on one side and small bricks on the other?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: This is my balance scale. I put 8 blocks on this side, and 5 blocks on that side. Whoa! It tipped right over!
The side with more blocks is heavier, so it goes down. The side with fewer blocks goes up. Let's add blocks to the light side, one at a time, and watch.
8 and 8. Now it balances, perfectly flat. When both sides are the same, we use the equals sign: 8 equals 8.

Now take some away from this side. 8 on the left, 5 on the right. The sign's wide open side faces the bigger amount, and its point faces the smaller one. This one means greater than: 8 is greater than 5.
And the other way: 3 on the left, 6 on the right. The open side faces the 6. This one means less than: 3 is less than 6.

Now a challenge. 15 blocks on the left. On the right you can use big blue 5-blocks and small yellow 1-blocks. Choose how many 5-blocks to use, tap the hammer, and I'll fill up the rest with 1-blocks. How many different ways can you balance it?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: I wrote 8, then the sign, then 5. The point is next to the 8, so I'm saying 8 is less than 5!

question.prompt: Is Steve right that 8 is less than 5?
question.onRight: Yes, you caught it. 8 is more than 5, so the open side should face the 8.

0.mistake: reads the sign the wrong way round
0.hint: Which side would go down on the scale: 8 blocks or 5 blocks?
0.say: 8 blocks are heavier than 5, so the 8 side goes down. The open side of the sign faces the bigger number, 8. So 8 is greater than 5.

question.reveal: 8 is greater than 5. The open side faces the 8.

rule.text: The open side faces the bigger amount.
rule.ask: Can you say how to tell which way round the sign goes? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: Heavier goes down. The same balances, and that's equals. The open side of the sign faces the bigger amount.

bonus.prompt: Bonus: with 10-blocks, 5-blocks and 1-blocks, how many ways could you balance 20? Guess!
bonus.reveal: 9 ways! Adding a new size of block makes lots more mixes.
